entities.summary: Captain Samuel Wallis was a Royal Navy officer and explorer who made the first recorded visit by a European navigator to Tahiti on 28 October 1767. This voyage marked a pivotal moment in the history of Pacific exploration and had significant consequences for the indigenous populations of Tahiti and the surrounding islands. Wallis's expedition also laid the groundwork for subsequent European explorations of the Pacific, including those of James Cook. The legacy of Wallis's voyage can be seen in the maps and charts that were created during this period, which continue to be studied by historians and cartographers today. Notably, Wallis's account of his voyage, which included detailed descriptions of the natural history and culture of Tahiti, remains an important primary source for understanding the history of the Pacific Islands during this period.
